items.q:
The Indian citizenship of a person can be terminated if
I. the person voluntarily acquires the citizenship of some other country.
II. the person has become a citizen through registration.
III. the Government of India is satisfied that citizenship was obtained by fraud.
IV. a citizen by birth indulges in trade with an enemy country during war.
o: I, III and IV are correct
I, II and III are correct
items.x: I is termination; III is deprivation. Becoming a citizen by registration is not itself a ground, and deprivation (including for trading with the enemy) applies only to citizens by registration or naturalisation, not to citizens by birth.

items.q: Name the types of citizens.
items.a: Natural citizens (citizens by birth) and naturalised citizens (those who acquire citizenship).

items.q: What are the rights that a citizen can enjoy in our country?
items.a: Fundamental Rights; the right to vote in Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections; the right to hold certain public offices; and the right to become a Member of Parliament or of a State Legislature.

items.q: Mention any three qualities of a good citizen.
items.a: Loyalty to the Constitution; obeying the laws; contributing to society and performing civic duties; respecting diversity; honesty and justice.

items.q: Name the five ways of acquiring citizenship.
items.a: By birth, by descent, by registration, by naturalisation and by incorporation of territory.

items.q: What do you know about the Citizenship Act of 1955?
items.a: The Citizenship Act, 1955, passed by Parliament under Article 11, provides for the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship. It prescribes five ways of acquiring citizenship and three ways of losing it (renunciation, termination and deprivation). It has been amended several times (1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019).

items.q: On what grounds is the citizenship of a person cancelled?
items.a:
1. Renunciation: a voluntary act by which an Indian citizen who has acquired another country's citizenship gives up Indian citizenship by declaration.
2. Termination: by operation of law, when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country, he or she automatically ceases to be an Indian citizen.
3. Deprivation: compulsory termination by an order of the Government of India if citizenship (by registration or naturalisation) was obtained by fraud or false representation, the person is disloyal to the Constitution, has traded or communicated with the enemy during war, has been imprisoned for two years within five years of registration or naturalisation, or has lived outside India continuously for seven years.
